question.text: A club deal is being formed by three Cat II AIFs to take 'Bharat Consumer Products Ltd.' private via a delisting offer. The target is a listed, cash-generative, under-leveraged mid-cap. Which buy-out archetype is MOST likely to be structured here?

answer.text: Management Buy-In (MBI) with totally new external team
Venture Capital Series-A round with founder top-up
Pure growth-capital PE round with minority stake
Leveraged Buy-Out (LBO) where significant acquisition debt is raised against target cashflows

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Chapter 8.3.1.2: LBOs are triggered when a cash-generative target with low leverage is acquired — free cashflows service the new debt, juicing ROE. The target described matches the classic LBO template (typically 70% debt, 30% equity). **The Trap:** Option A (MBI) is rare in India and requires the external team to lead the buyout, not three AIFs. Option C contradicts the control/delisting objective. Option D (Series-A) applies to early-stage, not mature cash-cow targets. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-C covers LBO mechanics at Manager level; XIX-A/B treat LBOs only in descriptive distributor terms. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** When modelling LBO returns, stress-test debt-servicing under a 30% EBITDA decline — 70% leverage is unforgiving, and ratings downgrades of the SPV can trigger covenant defaults.
